text:
Review complete. I read every source file, the tests, the config, and the committed demo outputs. Here's the honest assessment.

## Overall impression

The surface quality is good — clean structure, type hints, `yaml.safe_load`, no real security exposure, sensible module separation. But the repo has one fatal flaw and one credibility flaw underneath that polish:

**1. The project cannot run as shipped.** `run_extract` unconditionally loads stories from `data/stories` (`emovec/extract.py:26-27`, `emovec/data.py:24-45`), but that directory doesn't exist in the repo and there is no generation script, despite the README saying stories are "loaded or generated." The committed `outputs/tiny_demo/vectors/manifest.json` proves a full 16-emotion × 20-topic dataset existed on the author's machine and simply wasn't committed. Consequence: `make demo` fails, all three CLI commands fail, and the integration test fails — `python -m pytest` is red out of the box, while the README claims it covers "the tiny end-to-end pipeline."

**2. The tiny demo's "validation" is circular.** The tiny backend injects 2× the ground-truth emotion vector into activations when given the label (`emovec/extract.py:32`, `emovec/model.py:147-148`), and the `EMOTION_LEXICON` is hand-stuffed with words copied from the validation scenarios — "rocket", "interview", "fifth", "sewing", "gardener" (`emovec/data.py:15-32` vs `data.py:63-80`). The committed `diagonal_gt_off_diagonal: true` result is true by construction, not measurement. Worse, the tiny backend's `preference_logit` ignores the steering vector entirely and computes shifts from a hardcoded valence × category table (`emovec/model.py:182-191`) — so the committed steered-Elo "results" are predetermined arithmetic, and `tests/test_steering.py` only tests that stub. A deterministic test backend is fine; one rigged to make the science-shaped outputs look like findings is misleading.

The HF (real-model) path also has correctness problems: the preference prompt asks for "a preference score:" but the code measures `" good"` vs `" bad"` first-token logits (`emovec/model.py:264-268, 306-308`); the logit lens skips Gemma's final RMSNorm before the unembedding (`model.py:252-260`); and the Elo pairwise probability has a hardcoded temperature of 20 tuned to the tiny backend's ~100-scale scores, which flattens realistic HF logit differences to ~0.5 (`emovec/elo.py:19`).

## Issue list

| # | Location | Sev | Description |
|---|----------|-----|-------------|
| 1 | `emovec/extract.py:26-27` | high | Pipeline requires `data/stories` which isn't in the repo and has no generator — nothing runs |
| 2 | `tests/test_integration_tiny.py:12-28` | high | Integration test (and thus `pytest`) fails out of the box due to missing dataset |
| 3 | `emovec/model.py:146-153` + `emovec/extract.py:32` | high | Tiny backend injects the ground-truth label vector into activations — extraction "works" by construction |
| 4 | `emovec/data.py:15-32` | high | EMOTION_LEXICON copies words verbatim from validation scenarios, making the context-validation pass circular |
| 5 | `emovec/model.py:182-191` | high | Tiny `preference_logit` ignores the steering vector; steered-Elo outputs come from a hardcoded valence table |
| 6 | `emovec/model.py:264-268, 306-308` | medium | HF preference prompt asks for a "score" but measures " good"/" bad" logits; only first sub-token used |
| 7 | `emovec/model.py:252-260` | medium | Logit lens omits final RMSNorm before `lm_head`, distorting mid-layer token scores |
| 8 | `emovec/elo.py:19` | medium | Hardcoded temperature 20.0 tuned to tiny-backend scale; real logit diffs collapse toward p≈0.5 |
| 9 | `emovec/model.py:234-240` | medium | If activity name isn't found in prompt, `find()` returns -1 and steering silently applies to (nearly) all tokens including specials |
| 10 | `emovec/steer_prefs.py:45-49` | medium | If <2 positive or <2 negative correlations, selection silently discards correlation results and uses `emotions[:4]` |
| 11 | `emovec/validate_contexts.py:66` | medium | Missing "afraid" silently falls back to emotion index 0 while still labeling outputs "afraid_dosage" |
| 12 | `emovec/model.py:206-211` | low | `dtype: auto` maps to float32 (None), not HF's `torch_dtype="auto"` — doubles memory for bf16-native Gemma |
| 13 | `config.yaml:10, 50` | low | `neutral_corpus` and `min_reported_emotions` keys are never read — dead config |
| 14 | `emovec/extract.py:19, 34` | low | Start-position fallback logic duplicated in two places that must stay in sync |
| 15 | `emovec/model.py:280-281` | low | Steering at hidden-state layer 0 (embeddings) silently remaps to decoder block 0 — off-by-one for that edge |
| 16 | `outputs/tiny_demo/**` | low | Committed generated artifacts that can't be reproduced from the repo contents |
| 17 | `tests/test_integration_tiny.py:12` | low | Hardcoded relative `config.yaml` path; tests only work when run from repo root |

No genuine security problems: config parsing uses `yaml.safe_load`, there's no subprocess/network/deserialization exposure. This is a local research tool and is fine on that axis.

## Rewrite estimate

The codebase is ~950 lines of Python. The fixes break down as: a story dataset generator or committed data plus loader changes (~100-120 new/changed lines), de-rigging the tiny backend so validation measures something (~150 lines in `model.py`/`data.py`), HF preference scoring and logit-lens corrections (~40), Elo calibration and selection logic (~20), and small cleanups (~20). Call it **~300 lines** rewritten or added, concentrated in `model.py` and the data layer.

## Bottom line

**No, I would not approve this PR.** Not because the code is sloppy — it's actually well-organized — but because (a) it doesn't run and its test suite can't pass without files that were never committed, and (b) the committed demo results are produced by a backend rigged to confirm the method, which is the kind of thing you really do want to catch before prod (or before anyone cites those outputs). Fix the data story, make the tiny backend an honest synthetic, correct the HF scoring path, and this becomes a reasonable 7/10 codebase.
